clue.text: Loading area number two reported new delivery

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so we go by the sound of the words

parts.note: a loading bay
B is second in the alphabet, as in plan B
said aloud, bay-bee

explanation.surface: A warehouse announcement that a second consignment has arrived at the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all goods-in logistics; the delivery the definition means is a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is what a mother delivers, so a new delivery.

clue.text: Cheap lager? Add to basket

parts.note: an adjective for low-priced goods, as airlines and hotels are sold
Bud, short for Budweiser, a brand of lager
to get something is to add it to your shopping

explanation.surface: An online shopper popping a bargain beer into their basket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the brand name: BUD is Budweiser, and adding it to the basket means you GET it.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget as an adjective means low-priced, cheap.

clue.text: Republican in group eats at a funny time

indicators.note: the letter for Republican goes in the word for group

parts.note: a bunch is a group
R = Republican, placed inside the group word after its first letter

explanation.surface: A party member in some clique grabs a meal at an odd hour.
explanation.walkthrough: "Eats" reads as a verb, but here it is the slang noun for food: brunch is eats taken at a funny time, between breakfast and lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a meal eaten at an in-between hour, neither breakfast nor lunch.

clue.text: Cold, tender spot in heel checked for sensitivity

parts.note: C = cold, on taps

indicators.note: the tender spot goes inside the word for heel

parts.note: the heel of a loaf is its end
a sore is a tender spot, placed in END: EN(SORE)D

explanation.surface: A chilly, blistered heel being examined for how much it hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sensitivity" and "tender" pull toward a sore foot; the definition means material vetted for anything that could offend.
explanation.definitionFit: Censored material has been checked and cut for anything sensitive.

clue.text: Nearly all large parts shortened about 20 inches

indicators.note: keep all but the last letter

parts.note: cut = shortened
BIG without its last letter, set between CU and T

explanation.surface: Most big pieces have been trimmed down to around twenty inches.
explanation.walkthrough: "Parts" looks like a noun belonging to "large"; it is the verb, BI parting CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The cubit was an ancient measure, forearm length, of roughly 18 to 21 inches.

clue.text: Whinge at drunken Romeo's snoring habit?

indicators.note: the letters stagger about into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about a drunk called Romeo who keeps snoring.
explanation.walkthrough: A habit here is clothing, as a monk's habit is: what you wear to bed and snore in. The question mark marks that stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is the clothing, the habit, worn while sleeping and snoring.

clue.text: English company incorporated by professed animal killer traded freely

indicators.note: the English company is taken inside the professed animal killer

parts.note: openly declared
a hunter kills animals; E and CO go in after its H
E = English
CO = company

explanation.surface: A British firm taken over by an avowed hunter, its shares then freely dealt.
explanation.walkthrough: The professed animal killer is broken open after its first letter so the English company can sit inside. Over-the-counter trading happens directly between parties, outside a formal exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-the-counter securities are traded directly between parties, freely, off the exchange.

clue.text: Paint large bird and small that cat's caught

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird
a lion is a big cat
S = small, caught inside LION: L(S)ION

explanation.surface: An instruction to paint a big bird and the little one the cat got.
explanation.walkthrough: "Paint" reads as an order to an artist; it is the noun, emulsion being the everyday wall paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is water-based paint used on walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Criminal here stood for sharing wealth, primarily

definitions.text: Criminal here stood for sharing wealth, primarily

indicators.note: the letters are made crooked, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: take the first letters of sharing and wealth

parts.note: first letters of sharing and wealth

explanation.surface: A historical note on where a famous outlaw lived who stood for redistributing wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Robin Hood, the outlaw who robbed the rich to give to the poor, made his home in Sherwood Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire is legendary home of Robin Hood, the criminal who shared out wealth.

clue.text: Awful blister that hurt in bed after Georgia rolled over

indicators.note: GABED is turned round to DEBAG

parts.note: GA is the US state abbreviation
after GA: GABED, then turned round to DEBAG
what you say when something hurts, set in after the first letter

explanation.surface: A painful blister makes a night in a Georgia bed miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: "Blister" suggests a skin complaint; in slang it is an irritating person, so the definition is an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Douchebag is slang for a contemptible person, an awful blister.

clue.text: Supply crack online?

parts.note: E = electronic, as in e-mail
a crack is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Asking where to get hold of drugs on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at drugs; crack here is a wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to supply them with what they need.

clue.text: Operation involving subs going north not what it seems

indicators.note: in a down answer, going north turns the letters upward, reversing them

parts.note: OP = operation
subs = subscriptions, dues; placed inside OP before the whole is reversed

explanation.surface: A naval operation with submarines heading north that is not what it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: "Subs" suggests submarines; it is short for subscriptions, dues paid to a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means sham, not what it appears to be.

clue.text: Bit of work first for recycler, leaving out bottles

parts.note: except = leaving out

indicators.note: take the first letter of recycler

parts.note: first letter of recycler, held inside the phrase for leaving out

explanation.surface: A recycler's first job is to sort out the glass bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bottles" looks like the recycling; it is a verb, holding the R in.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken from a longer work.

clue.text: Where "Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans…" leads? (As You Like It)

definitions.text: Where "Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans…" leads
definitions.meaning: Jaques's seven ages speech: the next item in the list after eyes
a recipe phrase meaning in whatever amount you prefer

explanation.surface: A quotation from Jaques's speech on the seven ages of man, with its play named.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a source reference; it is the second definition. The line in As You Like It runs "Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans taste, sans everything".
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the next word of Jaques's line is the flavour sense, and a cook seasoning by that sense adds as much as you like.

clue.text: Perhaps keep string to wrap present officially

indicators.note: a fort is one example of a keep

parts.note: a keep is a castle stronghold, a fort for example
present = here, as in a register
cord is string

explanation.surface: Advice to hang on to the string from a gift you are wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: "Present" reads as a gift to wrap; it means here, as in answering a register, and the keep and the string wrap it from either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something for the record puts it on the official record.

clue.text: Sinner top sort of this?

indicators.note: sort as a verb: sort the letters into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer at the top of a class of wrongdoers.
explanation.walkthrough: Jannik Sinner is the Italian world number one tennis player, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: Jannik Sinner is the world's leading tennis professional, so the whole clue reads straight as a description of the answer.

clue.text: Funny sitrep entertaining intelligence

indicators.note: the letters are in a funny, odd order

parts.note: anagram fodder; a sitrep is a military situation report

explanation.surface: An amusing situation report full of military intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: "Intelligence" reads as military information to go with sitrep; the definition means lively wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively, amusing wit: entertaining intelligence.

clue.text: Lover bound architect's splayed ribs

parts.note: a lover of something is a fan
to bound or leap is to vault

explanation.surface: A lover leaping over an architect's splayed ribs, as if in a strange accident.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ribs" suggests a body; these are an architect's stone ribs spreading out like a fan across a ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan vault is a ceiling whose ribs spread out from each column like an opened fan.

clue.text: Space on packed bus replacement service for jilted bride?

definitions.meaning: where you stand when the seats are full
split the answer after STAND: a stand-in for the absent groom

explanation.surface: A rail replacement bus so crammed it seems to be full of wedding guests.
explanation.walkthrough: "Replacement service" reads as the bus that stands in for a train; read STANDING ROOM as STAND-IN GROOM and the jilted bride has her substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing room is the space left for standing passengers when a bus is full.

clue.text: Index for one name

definitions.meaning: the index is the pointing digit, one example of the class
to identify someone to the police as the culprit

explanation.surface: A note that an index is one kind of list of names.
explanation.walkthrough: "Index" suggests the back of a book; here it is the pointing finger. To finger a suspect is to name them.
explanation.definitionFit: Finger as a verb means to identify or name someone, usually as guilty.

clue.text: Characters edging over East River in New York habitually cross there

indicators.note: take the letters on the edges of over

parts.note: the outer letters of over
NY = New York
E = East, inside NY
R = River, inside NY after E: N(ER)Y

explanation.surface: New Yorkers crossing the East River, as they do every day.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cross" looks like crossing the river; it means bad-tempered. "There" signals the word is American, ornery being US dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornery is American for cantankerous, habitually bad-tempered.

clue.text: Artist and half orchestral players stuffed envelopes

indicators.note: keep half the letters of violinists

parts.note: RA = Royal Academician
the first half of VIOLINISTS

explanation.surface: A painter and some orchestra members sit stuffing envelopes for a mailing.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stuffed envelopes" reads as office work; ravioli are little pasta envelopes stuffed with filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small pasta parcels, envelopes of dough with a stuffing.

clue.text: On the way back, strap down load on bike

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rein is a strap
the nap on cloth is its soft down; REINNAP is then read backwards

explanation.surface: A cyclist on the return trip straps their luggage onto the bike.
explanation.walkthrough: "Down" looks like a direction for strapping; it means the soft fluff or nap of a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a bag carried on a bicycle rack, a load on a bike.

clue.text: Place just a train ride from London remains sub-standard

definitions.text: Place just a train ride from London

parts.note: in golf the standard score for a hole
to remain is to be, placed under PAR

explanation.surface: A complaint that some place near London stays below standard.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sub-standard" reads as one word meaning poor; split it, sub is the instruction to put IS under PAR. Paris is a Eurostar ride from London.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is reached from London by the Eurostar train through the Channel Tunnel.

clue.text: Conservative blocks loyal campaigners' suspension

parts.note: true = loyal
C = Conservative, set inside the word for loyal

explanation.surface: A Tory politician gets faithful party campaigners suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: "Suspension" suggests a disciplinary ban; it is a suspension of fighting between warring campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a suspension of hostilities between those campaigning against each other.

clue.text: Darwin's ship led by sound of miserable shark

indicators.note: we want a spelling that sounds like the word for miserable

parts.note: poor = miserable
HMS Beagle carried Darwin round the world

explanation.surface: An account of Darwin's voyage being shadowed by a sorrowful-sounding shark.
explanation.walkthrough: The porbeagle is a North Atlantic shark; its first syllable is pronounced like poor.
explanation.definitionFit: The porbeagle is a mackerel shark of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Irish drunk promises to pay after second dram

parts.note: S = second
a dram or tot is a small measure of spirits
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A drunk Irishman offers to settle up after another whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: Stotious is Irish slang for very drunk, and "Irish drunk" is an adjective meaning that, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: the word is Irish (and Scots) slang for very drunk, so the definition names both the sense and where it is spoken.

clue.text: Host taking book from off his trolley

indicators.note: take away the letter for book
the book is taken from the word for off his trolley

parts.note: barmy = crazy; off one's trolley is British slang for mad
B = book, removed from the front of BARMY

explanation.surface: A party host who has lost his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: "Host" reads as a party giver; its older sense is a great number of soldiers, an army.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of host is a great body of soldiers, as in the heavenly host or Lord of Hosts.
